subject: CloudLeap trial: eval runbook, GPU commitments, and acceptance gates
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Tran <evelyn.tran@cloudleap.com>, Miguel Ortiz <miguel.ortiz@cloudleap.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Mar 2028 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: CloudLeap trial: eval runbook, GPU commitments, and acceptance gates

Evelyn / Miguel —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have shared expectations heading into the trial window. I pulled together the runbook and a first-pass resource ask; attaching the evaluation plan (PDF) and our GPU runbook spreadsheet.

Recap of what you asked for during the demo:
- 2 minute avg response SLAs for synchronous user-facing flows (expected p50/p95 targets)
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~120 active users, expected token rate ~1.2k tokens/sec during peak experiments
- Eval focus: latency, cost/token, and fidelity against your key prompt set (shipping app prompts)

Our proposed commitment for the 2-week trial:
- Reserved baseline: 4 A100-class GPUs (reserved capacity) to guarantee steady-state latency
- Autoscaling: up to +50% burst (2 additional machines) with 5-minute cold-start fallback to hosted variants
- KV/prefix caching enabled for repeat prompt patterns; warm-cache expectation after 30 mins of traffic

Success criteria / acceptance gates (your team + ours):
1) Avg response p50 <= 600ms and p95 <= 1500ms for the production prompt set at baseline load
2) Cost per 1k tokens does not exceed the agreed threshold (we'll surface burn reports daily)
3) No correctness regressions vs your evaluation harness (we'll run automatic A/B evals on sample prompts)

Next steps I propose:
- We lock the reserved capacity for the trial window (target start: 2028-03-20) — Marissa will send the resource reservation + invoice stub
- Technical sync: 60 minutes with your infra and ML teams next Wed 2028-03-14 (tech checklist + test dataset)
- You to send final prompt set and procurement PO (if needed) by 2028-03-16

Please confirm these items or flag edits. If you want a larger burst cap we can size that but it affects short-term cost and the invoice.

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

Attachments:
- cloudleap-eval-plan-v1.pdf (plan + acceptance criteria)
- redwood-gpu-runbook-v3.xlsx (resource sizing + autoscale knobs)
From: Evelyn Tran <evelyn.tran@cloudleap.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Miguel Ortiz <miguel.ortiz@cloudleap.com>, CloudLeap Procurement <procurement@cloudleap.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Mar 2028 20:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudLeap trial: eval runbook, GPU commitments, and acceptance gates

Sergio — thanks for the clear recap. This aligns well with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- The prod prompt set for evaluation is ~1.2k prompts (we'll provide as a CSV). Latency targets are important; those p50/p95 numbers look reasonable.
- For burst: can we confirm whether the +50% burst is immediate or if there's a queue/backoff window? Our benchmark includes sudden traffic bursts from a scheduled marketing test.
- Regarding cost target: procurement needs an estimate line-item for reserved baseline + potential burst overage so we can model runway.

Procurement note: we'll circulate a PO for the baseline reservation once we have an invoice stub and the HubSpot deal/contract link. Our target is to sign and start 2028-03-20 as you suggested.

We can do the technical sync 2028-03-14 at 10:00am PT — Miguel (infra) will join.

Evelyn
Head of Product | CloudLeap Systems
evelyn.tran@cloudleap.com

Subject: RE: CloudLeap trial: eval runbook, GPU commitments, and acceptance gates

Sergio / team —

Thanks — I exported a short invoice stub and the reservation terms and attached them to this thread (see redwood-gpu-runbook-v3.xlsx). Quick internal confirmations:

- Baseline reservation: 4x A100 equiv (reserved) for the 2-week window starting 2028-03-20; billing monthly pro-rated for the trial period.
- Burst policy: autoscale up to 2 additional nodes (same instance class) with a soft queue for additional requests after the burst cap. The burst brings ephemeral capacity online within ~75s (typical warmup for model weights + KV cache). We will enable graceful fallback to the hosted low-latency variant if queue grows beyond threshold to preserve user experience.
- Preview metrics we'll provide: per-route p50/p95, token burn, cache hit rate, and daily cost delta vs baseline.

Action items assigned:
- Marissa: send invoice stub and reservation confirmation to CloudLeap procurement by EOD today (attached).
- Dev: share the checklist + exact test endpoints and a short script to replay 1.2k prompts during the tech sync.
- Sergio: confirm HubSpot deal link + coordinate DocuSign for the trial terms.

We will also include a run-of-show for the first 48 hours (who to pager, escalation contacts) in the runbook.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
